stem.text: Why is the boiling point of ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, higher than the boiling point of phosphine, $\text{PH}_3$?

A.text: Ammonia molecules are polar; phosphine molecules are not.

B.text: Ammonia molecules have significant hydrogen bonding; phosphine molecules do not.

C.text: N–H covalent bonds are stronger than P–H covalent bonds.

D.text: There is one lone pair in each ammonia molecule but no lone pair in each phosphine molecule.
